How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide for creating a **GET** request to the *“get information of device connector versions”* API on a Cisco Nexus Dashboard running **version 6.3.1**. I’ve broken it into three parts: | Part | What you’ll do | Why it matters | |------|----------------|----------------| | 1️⃣ | **Open the Dashboard & locate the API** | You need to find the exact endpoint and any required headers. | | 2️⃣ | **Configure the request** | Set method, URL, query params, auth, and headers. | | 3️⃣ | **Send & inspect the response** | Verify you’re getting the expected JSON payload. | --- ## 1️⃣ Open the Dashboard & locate the API | Step | Action | Screenshot (optional) | |------|--------|------------------------| | 1 | Log in to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard UI. | | | 2 | In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“Developer”** → **“API Explorer”**. | | | 3 | In the API Explorer search bar, type **“device connector versions”**. | | | 4 | From the drop‑down list, select the API titled **“Get information of device connector versions”**. | | | 5 | The right panel will now show the API details:
• **Method:** `GET`
• **Endpoint:** `/api/v1/device-connector/versions`
• **Query Params:** `deviceId`, `status`, etc.
• **Headers:** `Accept: application/json`, `Content-Type: application/json` | | > **Tip:** If you can’t find the API, double‑check that you’re looking at the correct **API version** (e.g., `v1`) and that your user role has permission to view it. --- ## 2️⃣ Configure the request ### 2.1 Set the HTTP method & URL | Field | Value | Notes | |-------|-------|-------| | **Method** | `GET` | The API is read‑only. | | **URL** | `https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions` | Replace `` with your actual host (e.g., `nexus-dashboard.cisco.com`). | ### 2.2 Add query parameters | Parameter | Example | Description | |-----------|---------|-------------| | `deviceId` | `12345` | Optional – filter by a specific device. | | `status` | `active` | Optional – filter by status (`active`, `inactive`). | | `limit` | `50` | Optional – pagination limit. | | `offset` | `0` | Optional – pagination offset. | > **Note:** If you leave all params blank, the API will return all available connector versions (subject to pagination limits). ### 2.3 Set authentication | Auth Type | How to configure | |-----------|------------------| | **Basic Auth** | Username: `admin`
Password: `YourPassword` | | **Bearer Token** | Click **“Auth”** → **“Add Bearer Token”** → paste your token. | | **OAuth2** | Click **“Auth”** → **“Add OAuth2”** → follow the wizard. | > **Security tip:** Never expose your password or token in shared scripts. Use environment variables or secret vaults. ### 2.4 Add headers | Header | Value | Why it’s needed | |--------|-------|-----------------| | `Accept` | `application/json` | Tells the server you expect JSON. | | `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Required for POST/PUT; harmless for GET. | | `X-Cisco-Nexus-Dashboard-Client` | `DashboardUI` | Optional – identifies the client. | --- ## 3️⃣ Send & inspect the response | Step | Action | Expected outcome | |------|--------|-------------------| | 1 | Click **“Send”** in the API Explorer. | The request is dispatched. | | 2 | In the **Response** pane, you’ll see:
• **Status Code:** `200 OK` (or `400/401/404` if something went wrong).
• **Headers:** `Content-Type: application/json`.
• **Body:** A JSON array of connector version objects. | | | 3 | Expand the **Body** to view the JSON. Typical structure: | | | | ```json | | | | { | | | | "data": [ | | | | { | | | | "id": "cv-001", | | | | "name": "Connector Version 1.0", | | | | "releaseDate": "2024-01-15", | | | | "status": "active" | | | | }, | | | | ... | | | | ], | | | | "meta": { | | | | "totalCount": 120, | | | | "pageSize": 50, | | | | "currentPage": 1 | | | | } | | | | } | | | | ``` | | | 4 | If you see an error (e.g., `401 Unauthorized`), double‑check your auth credentials. | | --- ## Quick cURL example ```bash curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions?deviceId=12345&status=active" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -u admin:YourPassword # Basic Auth ``` > **Replace** `` and `YourPassword` with your real values. > **If you’re using a bearer token**, swap `-u admin:YourPassword` for `-H "Authorization: Bearer "`. --- ## Troubleshooting checklist | Symptom | Likely cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | `404 Not Found` | Wrong endpoint or API version | Verify the URL path (`/api/v1/...`). | | `401 Unauthorized` | Bad credentials or missing auth | Re‑enter username/password or token. | | Empty `data` array | No matching records | Remove filters or adjust `limit/offset`. | | `500 Internal Server Error` | Server issue | Contact Cisco support or try again later. | --- ### Final note Once you’ve verified the request works in the API Explorer, you can copy the generated **cURL** command or export the request to **Postman** for automated testing or integration into your own scripts. Happy querying!
